Built against [wamsoft/krkrz_dev](https://github.com/wamsoft/krkrz_dev) V2.6.5

- **Previews that play the scene**: the card beside a Replay tile, a Search row or a chart scene now plays the scene's opening lines as the story shows them, with a bar for how far it has gone; hold Ctrl (a controller's R2) to hurry it. On a touch screen a long press shows it
- **Sprite Mode, a stage of your own**: put several characters on the stage at once, drag them into place, turn them round, zoom them with the wheel, pick a pose's variation, type a line for one to say in a message window, put the panel away, and take a screenshot; on a desktop, your own pictures in the save folder's `backgrounds` folder go behind them
- **Favourite voices from the story**: press V to keep the voiced line on screen, or click its star in the backlog; the music room's voices have three playlists besides the favourites, a lock that keeps a line in its list, the speaker's face, a jump to the line's scene, and Play all
- **The music room's player**: Pause (a click on the record or Space too), a level meter, tracks played once, in order or shuffled, three playlists of tracks put in order by dragging, and a progress bar that moves smoothly now
- **Spoken greetings**: Config's Title Greeting picks who greets you on the title: Ai, Pip (in his own babble) or no one
- **The quick menu's buttons in your order**: Change Controls has a strip of them to drag into place
- **Scene moves in scripts KAG plays itself** (not compiled): back to the start of the scene, back to the last choice, rewind and on to the next scene, as in compiled scenes
- **Screen readers** read Config, save and load and Extras: each button and slider, named by its label or help line
- For game makers: `KAGSceneSteps` (`ScenePreview.tjs`), `KAGSpriteStageLayer`, `KAGFavouriteVoices` playlists and `KAGVoiceListPlayer` (`Voices.tjs`), `greetings.csv`'s Who column, `KAGQuickOrderStrip`, and `KAGMessageNodes`/`KAGA11yScreenNames` (`Accessibility.tjs`)
- kagex-release 0.25.0 downloads the 0.25.0 engines

The sample game with Live2D (`kagex_sample_live2d_<platform>`, added to this release once it's out) holds Live2D's Cubism Core: by installing or playing it you agree not to copy the Cubism Core out of it, distribute it apart from the game, modify it, or reverse engineer, decompile or disassemble it. It uses sample data owned and copyrighted by Live2D Inc.

Everything in this release is listed in [CHANGELOG.md](https://github.com/krkren/kagex/blob/0.25.0/CHANGELOG.md).

On Windows the engine needs OpenGL ES: a graphics driver that supports it, or ANGLE's `libEGL.dll` and `libGLESv2.dll` next to `krkrz.exe`.

The macOS app and tools aren't signed with an Apple Developer ID, so macOS blocks them the first time: open the app from the context menu (Open), or allow it under System Settings > Privacy & Security; for the tools, `xattr -d com.apple.quarantine kagex-release kagex-lipsync`. The Android APK is signed with a debug key: allow installs from unknown sources, or use `adb install`. The sample's iOS build is for the Simulator; kagex-release signs a game for iPhones and iPads with your own Apple Developer certificate.
